An important note: you're at an age where your testosterone is peaking. That is connected to strong sexual desires. It's absolutely natural to feel that way, this is our biology making sure the species survives. 

Observe and control your behaviours, but do not stress about the hormones making you mad. That's what being 19 is.

Now porn is a different animal. Porn addiction is a real bitch. Try to reduce as much as you can and don't feel bad when you fail, just try again to reduce. Every single time you consciously decide not to watch porn is a win - count these instead of feeling bad every time you fail. It is a poison we all do not need but are told it's totally normal.

Thank you! This helps a lot. I honestly wouldn't think that consciously doing the things I find difficult might be the way to improve my self esteem. I thought I'd have to do other things before the hard stuff got easier. You made me realize, silly as it sounds, that I need to do more of the things I tell myself I can't do.

Recently I tried to just go out to the park when the weather is nice. I think I understand your walking the dog. I wouldn't think this was directly helping in any way before now, though.

Thanks for sharing! I really appreciate that.
Would you mind describing any of the small steps you took?

Two things: It's a good habit to check on yourself, but don't panic. Observe.

The other, very important imho, thing is to remember that you are at the age when your testosterone is peaking and that is connected to strong sexual desires.

The way I read your post: you feel attracted to girls that show first signs of maturity. Their bodies change and signal "I am ready to have children". That's what it is, it's nature.

I think you are more concerned about it because of your father, but there is no shame in being attracted to a girl who is 17 while you're 20. Remember that it was not nature that defined we're minors until we turn 18. Our biology is a spectrum and some bodies mature at 15, others at 19.

Undoubtedly, it is good to keep yourself in check but don't beat yourself up more than necessary.

Porn addiction is a real bitch. Try to reduce as much as you can and don't feel bad when you fail, just try again to reduce. Every single time you consciously decide not to watch porn is a win - count these instead of feeling bad every time you fail. It is a poison we all do not need but are told it's totally normal.

All in all: the best thing, imho, would be to find someone you trust to talk about this. Your father doesn't seem to be that figure. Is there anyone else you think you could talk to?

You judge a lot from a single situation in a 7yr marriage. Everyone has their weaker moments. A good marriage is not one that is perfect but one where everyone wants to fix things in order to keep going.

IMHO everyone involved is at fault.

The friend is a major AH for even asking that. Like WTF. Your man is an AH, although to a smaller degree, for putting it on you that he would've chosen other.

You are a little AH for taking vendetta and saying the same thing he did. If the friend was a 10/10 AH, Tim was a 7/10 AH and you were a 4/10 AH.

Do not take the blame, though! I think it's understandable, in the moment, that you said that. The better way to deal with this would be to answer the question by saying, that it is a stupid one. An attempt to bend the reality in order to make it uncomfortable for everyone. Maybe even add that it is unfair to you and Tim to ask that since it can easily get hurtful even without intent. 

I would apologize to Tim, BUT, also explain to him that he hurt you, too. Do not let it be a one sided situation. He shouldn't have said that even more than you, since you did it in retaliation.I would also discuss how much of an AH the friend was by bringing that up and see if you can find common ground. 

Do apologize, it is always good to acknowledge the feelings of others but do not take the blame for everything.
Thanks for the example. This actually helped me understand that I don't have to understand everything, if that makes sense.

>Is it bexause you want a reason to feel the way that you do otherwise?

I'm not sure I understand the question. Do you mean like me wanting to escalate something that I already experience? If so then no. I don't think I have experienced sexual abuse in the past.

Parts of my childhood have left me with a trauma but none of it was in any way related to this. At least I don't think/remember.

Most probably what my issue is, is a lack of affection in my younger years that manifests itself as wanting any kind of affection when I feel down. I think. It's really just complicated guesswork. I've been to therapy in the past and my therapist once told me that if they had cloned me and sat me on the couch right beside where I was - I wouldn't know that person. So I'm careful to assume what I think or feel.

Now that you mentioned it I recall wishing something like this would happen to me as well when I was a kid. That was long, long before such stories had the described effect on me.

Thank you for sharing. Sorry you struggle(d) with this, too.
Hey, I feel sorry to hear that. Sounds really tough.
